tools.weight-loss-calculator.faqs.1.answ: Most medical professionals recommend losing 1-2 pounds per week for sustainable, healthy weight loss. Losing more than 2 pounds per week long-term can lead to muscle loss, nutritional deficiencies, gallstones, and a slowed metabolism. The calculator warns you if a deficit would put your daily intake below 1,200 calories (women) or 1,500 calories (men), which are generally considered the minimum safe intake without medical supervision.
tools.weight-loss-calculator.faqs.2.ques: What is the Mifflin-St Jeor formula?
tools.weight-loss-calculator.faqs.2.answ: The Mifflin-St Jeor formula is the most widely recommended equation for estimating basal metabolic rate (BMR). For men: BMR = 10 x weight (kg) + 6.25 x height (cm) - 5 x age - 5. For women: BMR = 10 x weight (kg) + 6.25 x height (cm) - 5 x age - 161. Research shows it predicts actual resting metabolic rate within 10% for most people, making it more accurate than the older Harris-Benedict formula.
tools.weight-loss-calculator.faqs.3.ques: Why does my weight loss slow down over time?
tools.weight-loss-calculator.faqs.3.answ: As you lose weight, your body needs fewer calories to maintain itself, meaning your TDEE decreases. This is called metabolic adaptation. A deficit that initially caused 2 pounds of loss per week may only produce 1 pound per week after significant weight loss. To keep losing at the same rate, you need to further reduce calories or increase physical activity. This calculator uses your current weight for estimates, so recalculate regularly as you progress.
tools.weight-loss-calculator.faqs.4.ques: How should I split macros for weight loss?
tools.weight-loss-calculator.faqs.4.answ: When losing weight, higher protein intake helps preserve muscle mass and keeps you feeling full. A common recommendation is 30% of calories from protein, 35% from carbohydrates, and 35% from fat. This calculator provides macronutrient targets in grams for each deficit level. Protein and carbs provide 4 calories per gram, while fat provides 9 calories per gram. Adjust the ratio based on your preferences and body response.
tools.weight-loss-calculator.faqs.5.ques: Is eating below 1,200 or 1,500 calories safe?
tools.weight-loss-calculator.faqs.5.answ: Going below 1,200 calories (women) or 1,500 calories (men) per day long-term is generally not recommended without medical supervision. Very low-calorie diets can lead to nutritional deficiencies, muscle loss, fatigue, hair loss, and metabolic adaptation that makes future weight loss harder. If the calculator shows your target falling below these thresholds, consider a more moderate deficit combined with increased physical activity.

tools.alimony-calculator.metadata.title: Alimony Calculator
tools.alimony-calculator.metadata.descri: Estimate spousal support based on income gap and marriage length.
tools.alimony-calculator.faqs.0.question: How is alimony calculated?
tools.alimony-calculator.faqs.0.answer: Alimony calculations vary by state. About 16 states have some form of formula or advisory guideline — for example, New York uses 30% of the payer's income minus 20% of the recipient's income (without child support). Illinois uses 33.33% of the payer's net income minus 25% of the recipient's net income. The remaining states use judicial discretion, where judges weigh factors such as marriage length, income disparity, age, health, and earning capacity.
tools.alimony-calculator.faqs.1.question: How long does alimony last?
tools.alimony-calculator.faqs.1.answer: The duration depends on your state and the length of the marriage. Texas caps alimony at 5-10 years maximum. Florida caps durational alimony at 50-75% of the marriage length (and eliminated permanent alimony in 2023). Massachusetts caps it at 50-80% depending on marriage length. For marriages over 20 years, many states allow indefinite or longer-term support. Several states have recently reformed their laws to limit alimony duration.
tools.alimony-calculator.faqs.2.question: What is the difference between alimony and spousal support?
tools.alimony-calculator.faqs.2.answer: They are usually the same thing — different states use different terms. "Alimony" is the traditional term. Some states use "spousal support" (California), "spousal maintenance" (New York, Colorado), or "maintenance" (Illinois). Pennsylvania distinguishes between "spousal support" (during separation), "APL" (during divorce proceedings), and "alimony" (after divorce). Formulas may differ between the types.
tools.alimony-calculator.faqs.3.question: Is alimony tax deductible?
tools.alimony-calculator.faqs.3.answer: No. For divorce and separation agreements executed after December 31, 2018, alimony is not deductible by the payer and is not taxable income for the recipient. This changed under the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. Pre-2019 agreements keep the old tax treatment (deductible for the payer, taxable for the recipient) unless specifically modified.
tools.alimony-calculator.faqs.4.question: Can alimony be modified?
tools.alimony-calculator.faqs.4.answer: In most states, yes — if there is a substantial change in circumstances, such as job loss, retirement, a significant income change, or the recipient becoming self-sufficient. However, certain types of alimony are not modifiable (such as Florida's durational or lump-sum awards). Alimony usually terminates when the recipient remarries and often when they cohabit.
tools.alimony-calculator.faqs.5.question: Does adultery affect alimony?
tools.alimony-calculator.faqs.5.answer: In some states, yes. Georgia and South Carolina bar an adulterous spouse from receiving alimony. North Carolina denies alimony to a dependent spouse who engaged in "illicit sexual behavior," but it must be paid if the supporting spouse did so. Virginia treats adultery as one factor. In no-fault states like California, adultery generally does not affect alimony.
tools.alimony-calculator.faqs.6.question: Which states award the most and least alimony?
tools.alimony-calculator.faqs.6.answer: The highest alimony estimates come from states like New York, California, and Illinois — all of which have formulas or guidelines that produce substantial awards when there is a large income gap. Texas and Indiana are the most restrictive: Texas caps alimony at $5,000 per month with strict eligibility, and Indiana limits it to only 3 years for rehabilitation purposes. Mississippi courts are also reluctant to award alimony.
tools.alimony-calculator.faqs.7.question: How accurate is this calculator?
tools.alimony-calculator.faqs.7.answer: For states with statutory formulas (New York, Illinois, New Hampshire, Colorado, Pennsylvania), this calculator closely follows the actual formulas. For states with caps (Texas, Florida, Massachusetts, Louisiana), it accurately applies the caps. For discretionary states, it uses the AAML (American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers) recommended guidelines as a rough estimate. Actual awards depend on many factors the calculator cannot capture, including judicial discretion, property division, health, earning capacity, and the standard of living during the marriage.
tools.alimony-calculator.guide.whatIs.ti: How the Spousal Support Calculator Works
tools.alimony-calculator.guide.whatIs.co: This calculator estimates spousal support (alimony) based on your state's calculation method, both spouses' incomes, and the duration of the marriage. It implements specific formulas in states with statutory formulas and uses professional guidelines in discretionary states.
tools.alimony-calculator.guide.howTo.sec: States like New York, Illinois, New Hampshire, and Pennsylvania have statutory formulas that produce specific amounts. For example, New York uses 30% of the payer's income minus 20% of the recipient's income (without child support).
States like Colorado, Arizona, and New Mexico have formulas, but judges can deviate based on case-specific factors.
States like Texas, Florida, Massachusetts, and Louisiana have no formula for calculating amounts but do have statutory maximums. Texas caps alimony at $5,000 per month with strict eligibility.

The remaining ~30 states use judicial discretion with no formula. This calculator uses the AAML recommended guideline (30% of the payer's gross income minus 20% of the recipient's gross income) as an approximation.
tools.alimony-calculator.guide.tips.cont: Many states tie alimony duration to marriage length. This calculator estimates duration based on your state's guidelines — for example, Florida caps durational alimony at 50% of the marriage length for short-term marriages and 75% for long-term ones. States like Texas have absolute maximum durations (5-10 years). For marriages over 20 years in most states, indefinite alimony remains possible.
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.metadata.des: Determine Chapter 7 bankruptcy eligibility by comparing household income to state median income.
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.faqs.0.quest: What is the bankruptcy means test?
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.faqs.0.answe: The means test determines whether you qualify for Chapter 7 bankruptcy (debt discharge) or must file Chapter 13 (repayment plan). It compares your income against the median for your state and household size. If you are below the median, you pass automatically. If above, a detailed calculation using IRS standard deductions determines your disposable income.
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.faqs.1.quest: What income does the means test count?
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.faqs.1.answe: The means test uses your "current monthly income" (CMI) — the average of all income sources over the 6 calendar months before filing. This includes wages, commissions, bonuses, self-employment income, rental income, pensions, unemployment benefits, and alimony received. Social Security benefits are excluded.
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.faqs.2.quest: What if I fail the means test?
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.faqs.2.answe: If you fail, there is a presumption of abuse for Chapter 7. You can still file Chapter 13 (a 3-5 year repayment plan), or you can rebut the presumption by showing special circumstances (serious medical conditions, active duty, etc.). A bankruptcy attorney can help determine your options.
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.faqs.3.quest: How often do the median income figures change?
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.faqs.3.answe: The DOJ U.S. Trustee Program updates state median income figures about every 6 months based on Census Bureau data. This calculator uses the latest figures effective April 1, 2026. The disposable income thresholds ($9,075/$15,150) are adjusted every 3 years.
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.faqs.4.quest: What is the difference between Chapter 7 and Chapter 13?
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.faqs.4.answe: Chapter 7 discharges most unsecured debts (credit cards, medical bills) within 3-4 months but may require liquidating non-exempt assets. Chapter 13 creates a 3-5 year repayment plan based on your disposable income — you keep your assets but must make monthly payments. Chapter 7 requires passing the means test; Chapter 13 has debt limits (as of April 2025, $526,700 unsecured / $1,580,125 secured).
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.faqs.5.answe: The means test allows IRS standard living expense deductions (food, clothing, personal care), out-of-pocket medical expenses ($84/month under 65, $149/month over 65), transportation (ownership and operating costs), and actual expenses for housing, utilities, taxes, health insurance, childcare, and court-ordered payments. These deductions reduce your disposable income.
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.faqs.6.quest: Does Social Security count as income?
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.faqs.6.answe: No. Social Security benefits (retirement, disability, SSI) are expressly excluded from the means test income calculation under 11 U.S.C. § 101(10A). This is one of the most important exclusions — if your only income is Social Security, you automatically pass the means test.
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.faqs.7.quest: Can I still file Chapter 7 if I fail the means test?
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.faqs.7.answe: Possibly. Failing creates a rebuttable presumption of abuse. Special circumstances that may overcome the presumption include: serious medical conditions, active duty, or other documented events beyond your control that reduce income or increase expenses. Additionally, if your debts are primarily business debts (not consumer), the means test does not apply at all.
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.guide.whatIs: What Is the Bankruptcy Means Test?

The means test determines whether you qualify for Chapter 7 bankruptcy (debt discharge) or must file Chapter 13 (repayment plan). It compares your income against the median for your state and household size. If you are below the median, you pass automatically. If above, a detailed calculation using IRS standard deductions determines your disposable income.
The means test uses your "current monthly income" (CMI) — the average of all income sources over the 6 calendar months before filing. This includes wages, commissions, bonuses, self-employment income, rental income, pensions, unemployment benefits, and alimony received. Social Security benefits are excluded.

The means test allows IRS standard living expense deductions (food, clothing, personal care), out-of-pocket medical expenses ($84/month under 65, $149/month over 65), transportation (ownership and operating costs), and actual expenses for housing, utilities, taxes, health insurance, childcare, and court-ordered payments.

If your income exceeds the median, the calculator subtracts allowable deductions to determine disposable income. If your disposable income over 5 years is below $9,075, you pass. If it is above $15,150, you fail. Between these amounts, you pass only if disposable income is less than 25% of your non-priority unsecured debt.
tools.bankruptcy-means-test.guide.tips.c: This is a simplified estimate of the Chapter 7 means test. The actual means test (official Forms 122A-1 and 122A-2) includes additional deductions and line items not covered here. Median income data comes from the DOJ U.S. Trustee Program (effective April 1, 2026). Always consult a bankruptcy attorney for an accurate assessment.

tools.business-loan-calculator.faqs.0.qu: What is a good interest rate for a business loan?
tools.business-loan-calculator.faqs.0.an: As of 2026, a good rate for good credit is 6-10%. SBA loans run 7-9%. Traditional bank loans are 5-8%. Online lenders and alternative financing may be 10-25%+. Rates depend on credit, revenue, and time in business.
tools.business-loan-calculator.faqs.1.qu: What is the difference between business and personal loans?
tools.business-loan-calculator.faqs.1.an: Business loans are used for business purposes (equipment, working capital, expansion) and are typically based on business revenue and credit. Personal loans are for personal expenses and based on personal credit. Business loans may require a personal guarantee.
tools.business-loan-calculator.faqs.2.qu: What are typical business loan terms?
tools.business-loan-calculator.faqs.2.an: Working capital loans: 6 months - 2 years. Equipment loans: 3-10 years (matched to equipment life). Real estate loans: 10-25 years. SBA 7(a) loans: up to 10 years for working capital and 25 years for real estate.
tools.business-loan-calculator.faqs.3.an: Loans over $250,000 typically require collateral. SBA loans require collateral worth more than 25% of the loan amount. Equipment loans use the equipment as collateral. Lines of credit may be unsecured.

Can I deduct car loan interest?

Generally not, unless you are self-employed and use the vehicle for business. Interest on a personal car loan is not deductible. For business use: you can deduct the business-use percentage of the interest, or use the standard mileage rate.
When is car loan interest deductible?

If you are self-employed and use the vehicle for business (deliveries, client meetings, work errands), you can deduct the business-use percentage of the interest. Detailed mileage records are required.
What is the difference between the actual expense and standard mileage methods?

The actual expense method deducts the business-use percentage of vehicle costs (gas, maintenance, insurance, depreciation, loan interest). The standard mileage method uses an IRS-set per-mile rate (70 cents in 2026). Compare both to choose the better method.
No. Commuting from home to a regular workplace is a personal expense and not deductible. Only business-related errands (office to client, temporary work sites) are deductible.

tools.chatgpt-ads-calculator.metadata.de: Estimate impressions, clicks, and total spend for a ChatGPT ads campaign.
tools.chatgpt-ads-calculator.faqs.0.ques: How much do ChatGPT ads cost?
tools.chatgpt-ads-calculator.faqs.0.answ: ChatGPT ads currently cost about $60 CPM (cost per mille, or per thousand impressions), with a minimum commitment of $200,000-$250,000 for pilot programs. This makes ChatGPT about 3x more expensive than Meta ads (average $15 CPM) and about 12x more than Google Display (average $5 CPM). Pricing is expected to evolve as OpenAI introduces self-serve options (possibly in Q4 2026).
tools.chatgpt-ads-calculator.faqs.1.ques: What do ChatGPT ads look like?
tools.chatgpt-ads-calculator.faqs.1.answ: ChatGPT ads come in two main formats: (1) sponsored text links with a headline, description, and destination URL that appear below the AI response, labeled "Sponsored" with a brand favicon; and (2) product/shopping cards that show brand logos, product images, pricing, stock status, and action buttons in a scrollable horizontal layout. Video ads are not supported yet but are expected later in 2026.
tools.chatgpt-ads-calculator.faqs.2.answ: Currently, ChatGPT ads are enterprise-only and onboarded directly by OpenAI. There is no self-serve platform yet. A self-serve option is expected in Q4 2026. Interested advertisers can register at openai.com/advertisers. Minimum spend is about $200,000-$250,000.
tools.chatgpt-ads-calculator.faqs.3.answ: Ads are shown only to logged-in U.S. adults on the Free tier and the Go tier ($8/month). Users on Plus ($20/month), Pro ($200/month), Team, Business, Enterprise, and Education plans do not see ads. This limits the ad audience to free and low-tier users.
tools.chatgpt-ads-calculator.faqs.4.ques: How does ChatGPT ad targeting work?
tools.chatgpt-ads-calculator.faqs.4.answ: ChatGPT uses contextual targeting only, based on real-time conversations. There is no keyword bidding (like Google), no interest targeting (like Meta), and no demographic targeting. Advertisers never get access to individual conversations, chat history, or personal data. Only aggregated performance metrics (total views and clicks) are provided.
tools.chatgpt-ads-calculator.faqs.5.ques: Which brands are advertising on ChatGPT?
tools.chatgpt-ads-calculator.faqs.5.answ: Early advertisers include Target, Ford, Mazda, Adobe, Qualcomm, Expedia, HelloFresh, Williams-Sonoma, Audible, Mrs. Meyer's, and Audemars Piguet. Retail and grocery brands make up about 44% of early ChatGPT advertisers.
tools.chatgpt-ads-calculator.faqs.6.ques: How do ChatGPT ads compare to Google and Meta?
tools.chatgpt-ads-calculator.faqs.6.answ: ChatGPT ads are significantly more expensive per impression ($60 CPM vs. $5-38 for Google and $15 for Meta) but offer a unique contextual targeting model. Key trade-offs: ChatGPT ads reach users at high-intent conversational moments, but measurement is limited, format options are fewer (text links and product cards vs. full image/video/carousel), and there is no self-serve access.
tools.chatgpt-ads-calculator.faqs.7.ques: Are ChatGPT ads worth the cost?
tools.chatgpt-ads-calculator.faqs.7.answ: It depends on your goals. ChatGPT ads reach users at high-intent moments (actively asking questions about products/services), which may mean higher conversion rates. However, the $60 CPM and $200K minimum make it viable only for brands with significant budgets. Use this calculator to compare estimated ROAS across platforms against your specific conversion metrics.
tools.chatgpt-ads-calculator.guide.whatI: ChatGPT Ads: What Marketers Need to Know

OpenAI launched ads in ChatGPT in February 2026, creating an entirely new channel for brands. Unlike search ads (keyword intent) or social ads (interest-based), ChatGPT ads use contextual targeting based on the user's real-time conversation with the AI.
tools.chatgpt-ads-calculator.guide.howTo: Headline (about 60 characters) + description (about 180 characters) + destination URL, labeled "Sponsored" with a brand favicon. Appears below the AI response. The primary ad format.

Scrollable horizontal cards with brand logos, product images, names, prices, stock status, and action buttons (e.g., install, buy). Used for e-commerce and app promotion. Up to 3-4 scrollable cards per row.

Estimate monthly child support based on parent incomes, custody time, and number of children.
tools.child-support-calculator.faqs.0.an: Child support calculations vary by state but generally fall into three models. Income-percentage states (like Texas and Wisconsin) apply a fixed percentage to the non-custodial parent's income based on the number of children. Income-shares states (the majority) combine both parents' incomes, determine a basic obligation from a schedule, then split it proportionally. A few states like California use algebraic formulas that factor in custody time. All states also consider health insurance and childcare costs.
tools.child-support-calculator.faqs.1.qu: What is the difference between income shares and income percentage?
tools.child-support-calculator.faqs.1.an: Income percentage uses only the non-custodial parent's income and applies a fixed percentage. Income shares combines both parents' incomes to determine the total child-rearing cost, then assigns each parent their proportional share. Income shares is considered fairer because it reflects what would be spent on the children if the family were intact. About 41 states use income shares and 6 use income percentage.
tools.child-support-calculator.faqs.2.qu: Does custody time allocation affect child support?
tools.child-support-calculator.faqs.2.an: Yes, significantly. When the non-custodial parent has substantial custody time (typically 35% or more of overnights), most states reduce child support. The logic is that a parent who spends more time with the children directly bears more costs. Some states, like California, build custody time directly into the formula. A 50/50 custody arrangement usually results in a lower obligation, though the higher earner typically still pays something.
tools.child-support-calculator.faqs.3.qu: What income is included in child support calculations?
tools.child-support-calculator.faqs.3.an: Most states use gross income from all sources, including wages, salaries, commissions, bonuses, overtime, self-employment income, investment income, rental income, retirement benefits, and disability payments. Some states then deduct taxes and mandatory fees to arrive at net income. Income typically excluded includes means-tested public assistance (like TANF or SSI) and a new spouse's income.
tools.child-support-calculator.faqs.4.an: Yes, child support orders can be modified when there is a significant change in circumstances. Common reasons include a significant increase or decrease in either parent's income (typically 15-20% or more), a change in custody or parenting time, a change in the child's needs (medical, educational), or the child reaching adulthood. Either parent can file a motion to modify, and some states allow administrative reviews every few years.
tools.child-support-calculator.faqs.5.qu: What happens if a parent loses their job?
tools.child-support-calculator.faqs.5.an: Courts can impute income to a parent who is voluntarily unemployed or underemployed. This means the court assigns an income they could reasonably earn based on their education, skills, work history, and local job opportunities. If the job loss is involuntary and the parent is actively looking for work, the court may use actual income or unemployment benefits. Quitting a job just to reduce child support is generally not an effective strategy.
tools.child-support-calculator.faqs.6.qu: How long does child support last?
tools.child-support-calculator.faqs.6.an: In most states, child support lasts until the child turns 18 or graduates from high school, whichever is later. Some states extend it to 19 or 21. New York can order support until age 21. A few states allow support to continue through college graduation. Support can also end early if the child is emancipated (legally independent), joins the military, or marries. Disabled children may receive support indefinitely.
tools.child-support-calculator.faqs.7.an: No. Child support is never a tax deduction for the payer and is not taxable income for the recipient. This differs from spousal support, which was deductible under agreements made before 2019 but lost that treatment under the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. The parent who claims the child as a dependent gets the child tax credit — usually the custodial parent, unless the parents agree otherwise using IRS Form 8332.
tools.child-support-calculator.guide.wha: How the Child Support Calculator Works

This calculator estimates child support based on your state's calculation model, both parents' incomes, the number of children, and the custody time arrangement. It implements the three main calculation methods used in the United States.
tools.child-support-calculator.guide.how: The Three Child Support Calculation Models

Texas, Wisconsin, Mississippi, Alaska, Nevada, and North Dakota use this model. It applies a fixed percentage to the non-custodial parent's income. The percentage increases with the number of children. For example, Texas uses 20% of net resources for one child, 25% for two children, and up to 40% for five or more children. The custodial parent's income is not counted.

Most states (about 41) use this model. It combines both parents' incomes and uses a schedule to determine how much parents at that income level typically spend on their children. Each parent then pays their proportional share. Health insurance and childcare costs are added to the basic obligation.

California uses an algebraic formula (CS = K[HN - (H%)(TN)]) that directly incorporates custody time. New York uses Child Support Standards Act (CSSA) percentages applied to combined income up to a statutory cap. Delaware, Hawaii, and Montana use the Melson formula, which is similar to income shares but includes a self-support reserve.
tools.child-support-calculator.guide.tip: Actual child support calculations involve state-specific lookup tables with thousands of entries, judicial discretion, and dozens of additional factors this calculator cannot consider. These include extraordinary medical expenses, prior support obligations, visitation travel costs, tax filing details, and more. This tool provides a reasonable approximation to help you understand the possible range, but it should not be used as a substitute for legal advice.
tools.credit-score-simulator.metadata.de: Simulate how common credit actions affect your credit score.
tools.credit-score-simulator.faqs.0.answ: FICO score: payment history (35%), amounts owed (30%), length of credit history (15%), credit mix (10%), new credit (10%). VantageScore uses similar factors with different weights.
tools.credit-score-simulator.faqs.1.ques: What makes a good credit score?
tools.credit-score-simulator.faqs.1.answ: FICO scores range from 300-850. Good: 670-739. Very good: 740-799. Exceptional: 800+. A score of 670+ gets you approved, and 740+ gets you the best rates. Below 580 is considered poor and limits your options.
tools.credit-score-simulator.faqs.2.ques: How can I improve my credit score?
tools.credit-score-simulator.faqs.2.answ: Pay on time (the most important factor). Keep credit utilization below 30% (ideally under 10%). Don't close old accounts. Limit hard inquiries. Dispute errors on your report.
tools.credit-score-simulator.faqs.3.ques: What is the difference between hard and soft inquiries?
tools.credit-score-simulator.faqs.3.answ: Hard inquiries (loan applications) lower your score by 5-10 points for up to 2 years. Soft inquiries (checking your own score, employer checks, pre-approvals) do not affect your score.
tools.credit-score-simulator.results.pay: Paying down revolving debt can help your credit score.
tools.credit-score-simulator.results.onT: 6 months of on-time payments can help your credit score.
12 months of on-time payments can significantly improve your credit score.
tools.credit-score-simulator.results.mis: A 30-day late payment could lower your credit score.
A 90-day late payment could seriously damage your credit score.
tools.credit-score-simulator.results.har: A hard inquiry creates a small, short-term impact.
tools.credit-score-simulator.results.new: A new account may temporarily lower your credit score slightly.
tools.credit-score-simulator.results.max: Maxing out a card can significantly lower your credit score.
tools.credit-score-simulator.results.set: Settling a debt could lower your credit score.

tools.debt-to-income-calculator.metadata: Calculate your DTI ratio to assess loan eligibility and credit health.
tools.debt-to-income-calculator.faqs.0.a: Your debt-to-income ratio is the percentage of your gross monthly income that goes toward paying debts. Lenders use it to gauge your ability to manage monthly payments and repay borrowed money. A lower DTI means less risk to lenders and more borrowing power for you.
tools.debt-to-income-calculator.faqs.1.q: What is the difference between front-end and back-end DTI?
tools.debt-to-income-calculator.faqs.1.a: Front-end DTI (also called the housing ratio) only includes housing-related costs like mortgage or rent. Back-end DTI includes all recurring monthly debts: housing, car payments, student loans, credit cards, child support, and any other obligations. Lenders evaluate both, but back-end DTI is typically the deciding factor.
tools.debt-to-income-calculator.faqs.2.q: What is a good debt-to-income ratio for a mortgage?
tools.debt-to-income-calculator.faqs.2.a: For a conventional mortgage, lenders prefer a front-end DTI of 28% or less and a back-end DTI of 36% or less. FHA loans allow up to 43% back-end (sometimes 50% with compensating factors). VA loans have a guideline of 41% back-end but no strict front-end limit. Generally, keeping your DTI below 36% gives you the most options.
tools.debt-to-income-calculator.faqs.3.q: How can I lower my debt-to-income ratio?
tools.debt-to-income-calculator.faqs.3.a: You can lower DTI by paying down existing debts (especially high-payment ones like car loans or credit cards), increasing your income, avoiding new debt, or refinancing to lower monthly payments. Even paying off a single debt can significantly improve your ratio and mortgage eligibility.
tools.debt-to-income-calculator.faqs.4.q: Does DTI affect my credit score?
tools.debt-to-income-calculator.faqs.4.a: DTI itself does not directly appear on your credit report or affect your credit score. However, the factors that cause high DTI — like high credit card balances — do impact your credit utilization ratio, which is a major credit score factor. Reducing debt improves both your DTI and your credit profile.
tools.debt-to-income-calculator.faqs.5.q: Is gross or net income used for DTI calculations?
tools.debt-to-income-calculator.faqs.5.a: Lenders use gross income (before taxes and deductions) when calculating DTI. This is your total pre-tax salary, not your take-home pay. Self-employed borrowers typically use adjusted gross income from tax returns. This calculator uses gross monthly income for accurate lender-comparable results.

tools.dui-cost-calculator.metadata.title: DUI Cost Calculator
tools.dui-cost-calculator.metadata.descr: Estimate the total cost of a DUI, including fines, attorney fees, and insurance increases.
tools.dui-cost-calculator.faqs.0.questio: How much does a DUI cost?
tools.dui-cost-calculator.faqs.0.answer: A first-offense DUI typically costs $10,000-$25,000 or more (including fines, court costs, insurance increases, IID fees, DUI school, attorney fees, towing, and bail). Insurance increases alone average $5,000-$15,000 over 3-5 years.
tools.dui-cost-calculator.faqs.1.questio: How much does car insurance increase after a DUI?
tools.dui-cost-calculator.faqs.1.answer: Nationwide, insurance rates increase by about 88% on average after a DUI. North Carolina sees the largest increases at 300-400%+. California, Georgia, Hawaii, and Michigan increase 100-130%. Pennsylvania is the lowest at 30-50%. Increases typically last 3-5 years and can add $5,000-$25,000 or more to your total insurance costs.
tools.dui-cost-calculator.faqs.2.questio: Do I need a lawyer for a DUI?
tools.dui-cost-calculator.faqs.2.answer: While not required, a DUI attorney can often negotiate reduced charges, alternative sentencing, or dismissal. Attorney fees range from $2,500 for a simple plea to $10,000+ for a trial. Studies show that represented defendants get better outcomes in 70-80% of cases.
tools.dui-cost-calculator.faqs.3.questio: How long does a DUI stay on your record?
tools.dui-cost-calculator.faqs.3.answer: It varies by state. 11 states (including Alaska, Colorado, Kansas, Massachusetts, Oregon, and Texas) have lifetime lookback periods — meaning a DUI from decades ago still counts as a prior. Others range from 5 years (Alabama, Mississippi, Missouri) to 15 years (DC, Nebraska). Most states use a 10-year lookback period.
tools.dui-cost-calculator.faqs.4.questio: What is an ignition interlock device (IID)?
tools.dui-cost-calculator.faqs.4.answer: An IID is a breathalyzer wired to your vehicle's ignition. You must blow into it and register below a set BAC (usually 0.02-0.04) to start the car. Random retests are also required while driving. Cost: roughly $70-$150/month to rent, plus a $100-$200 installation fee. 34 states + DC require IIDs for all first-time DUI convictions.
tools.dui-cost-calculator.faqs.5.answer: SR-22 is a certificate of financial responsibility that your insurer files with the DMV proving you carry the minimum required coverage. It is not insurance — it is a filing. Most states require it for 3 years after a DUI. Any lapse resets the clock. The filing fee is $15-$50, but the real cost is the higher insurance premiums during the SR-22 period.
tools.dui-cost-calculator.faqs.6.answer: Utah lowered its legal BAC limit from 0.08 to 0.05, effective December 30, 2018, making it the strictest in the nation. Every other state uses 0.08. For reference, a 180-pound man could reach 0.05 after 2 drinks in one hour.
tools.dui-cost-calculator.faqs.7.questio: Is a first-offense DUI a felony?
tools.dui-cost-calculator.faqs.7.answer: In most states, a standard first-offense DUI is a misdemeanor. However, certain aggravating factors can elevate it to a felony: causing serious injury or death, having a minor passenger, an extremely high BAC, or multiple priors. Oklahoma's SB 54 (effective November 2025) makes certain first-offense DUIs felonies. Second or third DUIs are felonies in many states.
tools.dui-cost-calculator.guide.whatIs.t: How the DUI Cost Calculator Works
tools.dui-cost-calculator.guide.whatIs.c: This calculator estimates the total cost of a DUI/DWI conviction in all 50 states. It includes court fines, insurance increases, ignition interlock device (IID) fees, DUI school costs, towing, bail, and attorney fees (for first and repeat offenses).
tools.dui-cost-calculator.guide.howTo.se: Base fines are relatively low, but penalty assessments multiply the total. For example, in California the base fine may be $390, but with assessments the total reaches $1,560-$4,000+. DUI school adds $500-$1,800 depending on course length.

Nationwide, insurance rates increase by about 88% on average after a DUI. North Carolina sees the largest increases at 300-400%+. California, Georgia, Hawaii, and Michigan increase 100-130%. Pennsylvania is the lowest at 30-50%. Increases typically last 3-5 years.

Ignition interlock devices rent for about $70-$150/month, plus a $100-$200 installation fee. 34 states + DC require IIDs for all first-time DUI convictions. Additional costs include towing ($150-$300), bail ($500-$2,000), and attorney fees ($2,500-$10,000+).
tools.dui-cost-calculator.guide.tips.con: A first-offense DUI typically costs $10,000-$25,000 or more (including all costs). Insurance increases alone average $5,000-$15,000 over 3-5 years. This calculator provides estimates based on state regulations and average insurance data. Actual costs depend on your specific situation, BAC level, judge, attorney, and insurance company.
tools.home-affordability-calculator.meta: Calculate the maximum home price you can afford based on income, debts, and DTI limits.
tools.home-affordability-calculator.keyw: how much house can i afford
tools.home-affordability-calculator.faqs: Lenders use the 28/36 rule: housing costs should not exceed 28% of monthly income, and total debt should not exceed 36%. Affordability also depends on your down payment, interest rate, property taxes, and insurance.
How much should I put down?
Conventional loans require 20% to avoid PMI, but many buyers put down 3-5% (3.5% for FHA loans). A lower down payment means a higher monthly payment and PMI if below 20%.
How much house can I afford?

Rough rule of thumb: a house priced at about 2.5-3 times your annual income. Earning $80,000, aim for a price of $200,000-$240,000. But actual affordability depends on your debt, down payment, and current interest rates.
Property taxes (1-3% of home value per year), homeowners insurance ($1,000-$3,000 per year), maintenance (1-2% per year), HOA fees (if applicable), and closing costs (2-5% of the purchase price).

tools.income-percentile-calculator.metad: Estimate your income percentile by country.
What is the median household income in the U.S.?

The median U.S. household income is approximately $80,610 as of 2024. This means half of all households earn more and half earn less. Median is more meaningful than average because extremely high earners skew the average upward to about $114,000.
What income puts you in the top 1%?

A household income of roughly $600,000 or more puts you in the top 1% of U.S. earners. For individual income, the threshold is around $400,000. These figures are based on adjusted gross income from IRS and Census data.
What is considered middle class income?

The Pew Research Center defines middle class as households earning between two-thirds and double the median income. For 2024, that's roughly $54,000 to $161,000 for a household. However, cost of living varies dramatically by location — $80K in rural Ohio stretches much further than $80K in San Francisco.
Does this include all types of income?

This calculator uses total money income, which includes wages, salaries, self-employment income, Social Security, pensions, investment income, and other regular payments before taxes. It does not include capital gains, non-cash benefits, or one-time payments.
Why does household vs individual matter?

Household income counts all earners in a home. A household with two people each earning $50K has a $100K household income (68th percentile) but each individual is at the 57th percentile. Use household to compare family financial standing, individual to benchmark your personal earnings.
How does income percentile vary by age?

Income typically peaks between ages 45-54 when the median household income reaches about $97,000. Younger households (under 25) have a median around $40,000, while those 65+ have a median around $55,000. Your percentile relative to your age group may differ significantly from the overall percentile.

tools.life-insurance-calculator.metadata: Estimate recommended life insurance coverage using the income replacement method.
tools.life-insurance-calculator.keywords: how much life insurance do i need
tools.life-insurance-calculator.faqs.0.q: How much life insurance do I need?
tools.life-insurance-calculator.faqs.0.a: A common rule of thumb is 10-15 times your income, but a better approach is to calculate your needs: outstanding debts (mortgage, loans) + future expenses (college, living costs) - existing resources (savings, current coverage). The difference is the coverage you need.
tools.life-insurance-calculator.faqs.1.q: What is the difference between term and whole life insurance?
tools.life-insurance-calculator.faqs.1.a: Term life provides a death benefit for a specific period (10-30 years) and is cheaper. Whole life covers you for your entire life and builds cash value, but premiums are 5-10 times higher. Most people only need term life.
tools.life-insurance-calculator.faqs.2.q: How are life insurance premiums calculated?
tools.life-insurance-calculator.faqs.2.a: Premiums are based on age, health, coverage amount, policy type, and habits (smokers pay more). Younger, healthier individuals get lower rates. With term life, rates are locked in for the duration of the policy.
tools.life-insurance-calculator.faqs.3.q: Do I need life insurance through work?
tools.life-insurance-calculator.faqs.3.a: Employer-provided coverage is usually insufficient (often only 1-2 times your income). If you have dependents, add an individual policy to cover the gap. Individual policies stay with you when you change jobs.

Estimate annual Medicare costs, including premiums, IRMAA surcharges, and out-of-pocket expenses.
tools.medicare-cost-calculator.faqs.0.qu: How much does Medicare cost in 2026?
tools.medicare-cost-calculator.faqs.0.an: Most people pay $0 for Part A, and Part B is $202.90/month (standard premium). Part D averages about $39/month. Total baseline: about $242/month. Higher earners pay more due to IRMAA surcharges — up to $689.90/month for Part B alone at the highest income tier.
tools.medicare-cost-calculator.faqs.1.an: IRMAA (Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount) is a surcharge added to Part B and Part D premiums for higher-income beneficiaries. It is based on your MAGI from 2 years ago (2026 premiums use 2024 income). IRMAA kicks in starting at $109,001 for singles and $218,001 for married filing jointly. The highest tier (single $500K+, joint $750K+) adds $487/month to Part B and $91/month to Part D.
tools.medicare-cost-calculator.faqs.2.qu: Is Medicare Part A really free?
tools.medicare-cost-calculator.faqs.2.an: Part A is premium-free if you (or your spouse) worked and paid Medicare taxes for more than 40 quarters (10 years). With 30-39 quarters, you pay $311/month. Fewer than 30 quarters: $565/month. However, Part A still has a $1,736 deductible per benefit period, plus daily copays beyond 60 days.
tools.medicare-cost-calculator.faqs.3.qu: What does Medicare Part B cover?
tools.medicare-cost-calculator.faqs.3.an: Part B covers doctor visits, outpatient care, preventive services, medical equipment, ambulance services, mental health, and some home health care. After the $283 annual deductible, you typically pay 20% coinsurance with no out-of-pocket maximum — which is why many people buy Medigap supplemental coverage.
tools.medicare-cost-calculator.faqs.4.qu: What is the Part D out-of-pocket cap?
tools.medicare-cost-calculator.faqs.4.an: Starting in 2025, the Inflation Reduction Act set the Part D out-of-pocket cap at $2,000 per year ($2,100 in 2026). Once you reach this cap, you pay $0 for covered drugs for the rest of the year. This is a major change — previously there was no annual cap and costs could spiral.
tools.medicare-cost-calculator.faqs.5.an: Medigap (Medicare Supplement) plans are private insurance that covers the gaps in Original Medicare — copays, coinsurance, and deductibles. Plan G is the most popular, typically $100-$250/month depending on age, location, and insurer. Medigap only works with Original Medicare, not Medicare Advantage.
tools.medicare-cost-calculator.faqs.6.qu: What happens if I delay enrolling in Medicare?
tools.medicare-cost-calculator.faqs.6.an: Part B: a 10% premium surcharge for every full 12 months you were eligible but did not enroll — permanently. Part D: 1% of the base premium for every uncovered month ($0.39/month in 2026) — also permanent. These penalties add up fast: delaying Part B by 3 years means paying 30% more for life.
tools.medicare-cost-calculator.faqs.7.qu: When can I enroll in Medicare?
tools.medicare-cost-calculator.faqs.7.an: Your Initial Enrollment Period lasts 7 months: it begins 3 months before your 65th birthday month, includes your birthday month, and ends 3 months after. You can also enroll during the General Enrollment Period (January 1-March 31, with coverage starting July 1) or during a Special Enrollment Period if you have a qualifying event.
tools.medicare-cost-calculator.guide.wha: Medicare has several cost components: Part A (hospital), Part B (medical/outpatient), Part D (prescription drugs), and optional Medigap supplemental coverage. Most people pay $0 for Part A if they have more than 40 quarters of Medicare-covered employment. Parts B and D have standard premiums, which are increased by IRMAA surcharges for higher earners.
